builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
summary: RoboEvo$^2$ replaces human demonstration collection for adapting vision-language-action robot policies to unfamiliar tasks: a coding agent converts policy failures into reusable code/ICL/policy skills, and verified trajectories plus counterfactual preference distillation retrain the policy in a closed loop. The cost is a full robotics stack — simulation or hardware (LIBERO, RoboTwin, Unitree G1), policy supervised fine-tuning infrastructure, and an agentic search loop whose expense the paper only partially reduces. Failure modes include skill-memory consolidation of spurious fixes, counterfactual preference pairs that mislabel near-successes, and no evidence that gains transfer outside the evaluated robot benchmarks.
rationale: The method targets robot skill acquisition on physical or simulated robot platforms, which requires VLA policy training, robot hardware or simulators, and a coding-agent harness that fall outside the reader's stated production scope and budget.
technique: Recursive harness-policy co-evolution for robot self-improvement

claims.statement: RoboEvo$^2$ replaces human demonstration collection for adapting vision-language-action robot policies to unfamiliar tasks: a coding agent converts policy failures into reusable code/ICL/policy skills, and verified trajectories plus counterfactual preference distillation retrain the policy in a closed loop. The cost is a full robotics stack — simulation or hardware (LIBERO, RoboTwin, Unitree G1), policy supervised fine-tuning infrastructure, and an agentic search loop whose expense the paper only partially reduces. Failure modes include skill-memory consolidation of spurious fixes, counterfactual preference pairs that mislabel near-successes, and no evidence that gains transfer outside the evaluated robot benchmarks.

On LIBERO-PRO, standalone policy success rises from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% through recursive co-evolution, with reduced agentic costs on RoboTwin C2R and 95.0% hybrid success on Unitree G1-D.
